Suspected Gastritis.Symptoms: Many patients have no symptoms; Upper abdominal pain or discomfort; Nausea or vomiting; Early satiety or excessive fullness after eating; Loss of appetite or weight loss; Black or tarry stool, blood or coffee-ground material in vomit, fatigue, dyspnea, or light-headedness may indicate gastric bleeding
Suspected Gastritis.Risk Factors: Helicobacter pylori infection; Long-term exposure to NSAIDs, alcohol, or bile reflux; Autoimmune disease; Critical illness, sepsis, severe injury, or burns
Suspected Gastritis.Diagnostic Criteria: Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy with gastric biopsies can diagnose gastritis, determine its cause, and assess complications; Stool antigen or urea breath testing can identify Helicobacter pylori infection

Acute Gastritis.Diagnostic Criteria: Acute gastritis develops suddenly and lasts a short time; Gastric biopsy must show inflammation rather than mucosal injury with little or no inflammation

Chronic Gastritis.Diagnostic Criteria: Chronic gastritis develops slowly and lasts a long time; Helicobacter pylori and autoimmune gastritis are common chronic forms

Chronic Non-atrophic Gastritis.Diagnostic Criteria: Gastric histology shows chronic inflammation without the gland loss or intestinal metaplasia that defines atrophic gastritis; Evidence of Helicobacter pylori supports a common cause of chronic non-atrophic gastritis

Chronic Atrophic Gastritis.Diagnostic Criteria: Histopathology confirms loss of gastric glands, with or without intestinal metaplasia, in chronic inflammation; Intestinal metaplasia on gastric histology almost always implies atrophic gastritis; Endoscopic features may include pale thinned mucosa, increased vascular visibility, and loss of gastric folds
Chronic Atrophic Gastritis.Signs: Iron deficiency, vitamin B12 deficiency, or pernicious anemia may accompany corpus-predominant or autoimmune atrophic gastritis
Chronic Atrophic Gastritis.Risk Factors: Helicobacter pylori infection; Autoimmune gastritis and associated autoimmune thyroid disease
